Very glad to see this marvelous bakery re-open!
Jun 2020
The new Un Jour a Paris in District 3 has the same fine food as the old location.

My wife and I had been going to the previous location for many years, and were sorry (actually, devastated, in my case) when it closed.

I had one of my favorites, the Assiette Paysanne, and a glass of wine. Just as good as before. Went home with a baguette, a couple of croissants, and a pate creole.

The service was excellent; our waitress spoke flawless English.

This location is more convenient for us than the previous one, so I expect we'll be going there even more often.

A taste from France
Jan 2020
Une Journée à Paris deserves its name, as the place transports patrons to Paris, maybe not for a day as its name suggests, but certainly for the time they are there. While the pastries beckon those with a sweet tooth from the street, the salads and sandwiches are also quite tasty. We were there shortly after the new year, and were able to sample, or rather devour, a whole king’s cake for two. Traditionally called la galette des rois in French, it resembles a pie made of flaky dough (pâte feuilletée), stuffed with marzipan. Traditionally, there is a small object in it, which, when found by one of the individuals eating the cake, will designate him or her as the king or queen. This galette achieved a perfect equilibrium between flakiness and the density of the marzipan, all the while hitting the right amount of sweetness.
